This approach helps you avoid hazardous fire tiles clustered centrally, which are common obstacles. It’s important to practice small variations in the exact goal position near the top-right quadrant, as well as slight changes in fire placements around the center, to ensure the path remains robust. Keep your movements along the corridor just one row away from the fire except for the final descent, which minimizes the risk of colliding with fire. Demonstrations using this strategy have shown reliable success by maintaining a safe, consistent route that adapts well to different start, goal, and fire setups. Following this method strengthens the policy’s ability to generalize and avoid fire collisions effectively.
